gappers.catalyst: Q3 2026 beat before the open (EPS -$0.02 vs -$0.11 est; revenue $269.3M vs $245.9M FactSet est) three days after NASA awarded it a slot in the $10B CLPS 2 lunar program.
headlines: Intuitive Machines Expects 2026 Revenue Range $920M-$950M, Reports Q3 Revenue $269.3M vs FactSet Est $245.9M (MarketScreener)
Intuitive Machines, Inc. (LUNR) Reports Q3 Loss, Beats Revenue Estimates (Zacks)
NASA Awards Intuitive Machines Spot In $10 Billion Lunar Program (Benzinga, Nov 9)
Intuitive Machines Is No Longer Just About the Moon, CEO Sees Bigger Space Opportunity (Benzinga)
gappers.catalyst_detail: Intuitive Machines reported Q3 2026 at 07:30 ET, before the open. EPS came in at -$0.02 against a -$0.11 consensus (a +16.7% surprise per Zacks) and revenue was $269.3M against a $245.9M FactSet estimate (+10.7%). FY2026 revenue guidance was set at $920M-$950M, essentially in line with the $925.8M FactSet number rather than a raise. The print lands three days after NASA named the company to its $10B CLPS 2 lunar delivery program (Nov 9), and on the call the CEO reframed the story away from pure lunar landers toward broader space infrastructure-as-a-service. Benzinga shows short interest at 27.56% of float with 6.07 days to cover.
gappers.why: A genuine earnings beat on both lines, stacked on a $10B government program award, into a 27.6%-short float. The mechanism is primarily a short squeeze on top of a real fundamental catalyst: shorts positioned for another miss were forced to cover against a beat, and the CLPS 2 award gives covering shorts no obvious re-entry. Momentum buyers then chased the gap. Note the sell side is not confirming: B. Riley cut its target $43->$34 on Nov 4 and KeyBanc $38->$30 on Nov 2, both ahead of this print.
gappers.impact: Volume supports it: ~8.5M shares by 09:54 ET against an 8.33M full-day average, so roughly a full session of turnover in the first 25 minutes. That is real participation, not a thin headline pop. But the stock has already run from $8.62 (Nov 5) to $14.10 — +64% in five sessions, +22.9% in the last five closes alone — and it faded from a $14.35 open and a $14.62 high to $13.70 by 10:13 ET, so the gap is already leaking. Sector read-through is weak rather than confirming: this is Industrials / Aerospace & Defense, and XLI is +1.4% 1mo / -8.0% 3mo, one of the laggards, while the broad tape is in a defensive rotation (XLK -11.2% 1mo). No peer space name is moving with it; SATL (-5.5%) and ONDS (-5.2%) are both down today, which argues this is idiosyncratic to LUNR, not a space-sector bid.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: The CLPS 2 award and the guidance reset are structural, multi-year revenue events rather than a one-day headline, which is the LONG_TERM test. The caveat is that it does NOT align with the current sector-rotation phase in TRADING-STRATEGY.md: capital is rotating into Healthcare/Staples defensives, not Industrials, so the sector gate withholds endorsement even though the single-name catalyst qualifies.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Nothing to displace on the book — 0 open positions, $100k cash, 0% deployed, and 0 of 3 weekly trade slots used — so the cost is not a sold holding but the queued XLV $182-186 / XLP $89.00-89.50 / ABBV $285-288 pullback entries plus one of three weekly slots. The decisive problem is the 2:1 R:R gate: ATR(14) is $1.05, or 8.6% of price, so the mandated 10% trailing stop sits at just 1.16 ATR and would be taken out by a single average day's range. Clearing 2:1 against that stop requires a +20% target at $16.92, which is 2.7 ATR and above the entire post-gap range. Entering here also means paying up after a +64% five-session run with RSI 59 and the gap already fading intraday. It cannot clear 2:1 at a sane stop distance under the current rulebook.

headlines: Nebius Q3 earnings: revenue $980.8M, 2027 guide $12B-$13B, 2026 steered to low end, capex raised (ValueAddVC)
Nebius (NBIS) stock drops despite 571% AI revenue growth in Q3 2026 (Beinsure)
Nebius Group (NBIS) Surpasses Q3 Earnings and Revenue Estimates - surprises +149.18% EPS / +6.98% revenue (Zacks)
Nebius Q3 2026 Earnings Call: adj EBITDA margin 47.5%, prepayments cover >100% of contracted-capacity capex, site-timing risks (StockAnalysis transcript)
gappers.catalyst_detail: Nebius reported Q3 2026 before the open on Nov 12. Revenue was $980.8M, up 571% year over year and 8.4% above the $904.8M consensus of 17 analysts; adjusted EBITDA was $466M at a 47.5% margin against a nominal loss a year earlier; the EPS surprise was +149%. Management guided 2027 revenue to $12B-$13B and flagged Q4 pre-tax break-even. The damage came from the rest of the guide: 2026 revenue was steered to the LOW end of the previously issued $3.0-3.4B range, the 2026 capex plan was raised, and the call flagged site-timing risks on new capacity. The stock had closed up 15.44% at $154.69 on Nov 11 purely in sympathy with CoreWeave's print, so it entered today carrying expectations it had not set itself.
gappers.why: A textbook good-quarter / bad-guide de-rating, amplified by a borrowed starting point. Investors looked past a 571% revenue beat and priced the two forward items that change the capital story: revenue to the low end of the 2026 range plus higher capex means more cash burn per dollar of revenue and a larger future financing need. Because the stock had already rallied 15.4% on someone else's earnings, the beat was fully in the price and the guide had nothing to cushion it, so the move is a round trip of the sympathy gap rather than a reaction to a bad business.
gappers.impact: Volume is heavy and genuine at 27.0M shares, and the realized -15.1% move matches the ~14.9% implied move almost exactly, so options were correctly priced and this is an orderly re-rating rather than a liquidity break. It is not a one-day headline spike that mean-reverts: the repriced item is forward capital intensity, which persists until the next print. Sector read-through is direct and confirming — this is the same AI-infrastructure complex that is being de-rated across the board, with CRWV -6.5% today, XLK -11.2% over one month, and the unresolved NVDA governance crisis still sitting over the group. The quote is also disorderly right now (bid $120.00 / ask $134.40 at 10:13 ET), a $14 spread that makes any execution assumption unreliable.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: There is no durable long thesis to act on here: the structural news is negative (capex up, 2026 revenue to the low end) and the sector is in an active de-rating, so any long would be a mechanical bounce trade on a stock that just priced a worse capital path. It fails the LONG_TERM test and should not be carried.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Again nothing to sell to make room, but this name was already excluded by name in this morning's pre-market log as 'explicitly NOT a candidate' for exactly this setup, and today's outcome vindicates that call — so taking it now would spend one of three weekly slots on a setup the bot had already reasoned its way out of. The R:R is the worst on the board: ATR(14) is $16.39, or 10.6% of price, so a 10% trailing stop is 0.94 ATR — literally inside one average day's range, guaranteed to be gapped or noised through. A 2:1 target would need +20% to ~$157.67, which is back above the Nov 11 close the market just rejected. With the bid/ask $14 wide, slippage alone could exceed a meaningful fraction of the intended risk. No sane stop distance clears 2:1.

headlines: CoreWeave (CRWV) Q3 revenue rose 168% to $3.66B, above ~$3.55B consensus, backlog reached $132.5B from ~$104B in June (Threads/DailyMarketBrief)
CoreWeave Q3 Net Loss Widens, Revenue Rises - loss $1.27/diluted share vs $0.22 a year earlier (MarketScreener)
CoreWeave expects $13.0B-$13.3B 2026 revenue and targets $20B-$21B exit run-rate (UCapital)
CoreWeave Q3 2026 Earnings: Sold Out and Paying Up - active power 1.7GW, ~2.9x a year ago (Ren, Substack)
gappers.catalyst_detail: CoreWeave reported Q3 late on Nov 10: revenue of $3.66-3.7B, up 168% year over year and above the ~$3.55B consensus, with backlog expanding to $132.5B from roughly $104B in June and active power reaching 1.7GW, about 2.9x a year ago. Guidance was $13.0-13.3B for 2026 revenue with a $20-21B exit run-rate target. The offset was a GAAP net loss of $1.27 per diluted share, sharply wider than the $0.22 loss a year earlier, against a heavily debt-funded build. The stock entered the print at $48.73, popped roughly 16-25%, closed Nov 11 at $60.80, and is now unwinding that move for a third session.
gappers.why: Mechanical post-earnings profit-taking compounded by sector contagion. The fundamental news was good, so this is not a thesis break — it is holders monetizing a 25% two-day gain into a tape that has turned hostile to the AI-infrastructure trade. The contagion channel is specific: the WSJ report that Nvidia's board was preparing to force out CEO Jensen Huang is still unresolved, NVDA is -18.7% over nine sessions, and CRWV's economics are a leveraged derivative of exactly that GPU complex. The widening loss gives sellers a clean story to point at while they de-risk.
gappers.impact: Volume is the heaviest on today's board at 36.6M shares, so the unwind is broad rather than a thin drift. This reads as sustained rather than a one-day spike, because the driver is not a CRWV headline at all but an unresolved mega-cap governance event with a known forward date (NVDA earnings Nov 17) that can re-ignite it either way. Sector read-through is strong and confirming: NBIS -15.1% today on its own print, XLK -11.2% over one month, and this is the third straight session of give-back, which is distribution, not a single gap fill. The $132.5B backlog argues the business is intact; the tape argues nobody wants to own the financing risk right now.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: The backlog and power growth are genuinely structural, but the price driver today is a multi-day unwind inside an actively de-rating sector with a live binary (NVDA board, NVDA earnings Nov 17) overhead. Buying a falling knife in the weakest sector is a days-horizon trade against the rotation, not a swing hold, so it does not clear LONG_TERM.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Nothing to displace on the book, but this is the same name the 07:12 ET scan already ranked #1 and declined, so re-raising it costs a weekly slot on an idea already passed over twice today. R:R fails the same way as NBIS: ATR(14) is $5.73, or 9.4% of price, so a 10% trailing stop is 1.06 ATR and sits inside a single day's expected range in the middle of an active three-day unwind. A 2:1 target requires +20% to ~$68.18, which is above the Nov 11 close and roughly 2.1 ATR away, while the stock is trending down and the sector gate points the other way. Taking it would also concentrate the first position of a 90-day-flat book into the single weakest sector on the 1-month table, against a defensive rotation the bot has documented for two straight sessions. Cannot clear 2:1 at a sane stop.

headlines: Amprius Technologies Reports Wider Than Expected Q3 2026 Loss - GAAP net loss $0.02/sh vs $0.01 consensus (AlphaStreet)
Amprius Q3 Revenue Jumps 83% to $39.1 Million, Raises 2026 Outlook to ~$145 Million (Minichart)
Amprius Technologies falls 7% on third quarter earnings miss (Investing.com)
Amprius: Q3 Earnings Snapshot - loss of $3.5 million in the third quarter (WTOP/AP)
gappers.catalyst_detail: Amprius reported Q3 2026 on Nov 10. Revenue was $39.1M, up 83% from $21.4M a year earlier and comfortably ahead of the ~$35.9M consensus, and the company raised its full-year 2026 outlook to roughly $145M from at least $140M. The miss was on the bottom line: a GAAP/adjusted loss of $0.02 per share against a $0.01 consensus, a $3.5M net loss for the quarter. The stock fell about 7% on the print and is extending that today, a third session lower. The sell side remains constructive in aggregate — 15 Buy, 1 Hold, 0 Sell across 18 analysts with an average target of $23.14 against an $8.01 print.
gappers.why: A narrow bottom-line miss is being weighted over a clear top-line beat and a raised outlook, which is what happens to pre-revenue-scale growth names when the tape turns risk-averse. For a silicon-anode battery maker still losing money, a penny of extra loss reads as the unit economics not yet inflecting, and in a week where capital intensity is being punished across the board (see NBIS) that is the number the market chooses to price. The move is a slow bleed on light volume rather than a gap-and-go, so it is positioning drift, not a repricing event.
gappers.impact: Volume is the lightest on the board at 966k shares, which cuts both ways: the decline is not being driven by heavy institutional distribution, but it also means there is no capitulation flush to buy against. Against the stock's own history this looks closer to a drift than a one-day headline spike, and the five-day change of just +1.1% shows the name has gone nowhere while the rest of the board whipsawed. The bid/ask is tight at $8.15/$8.16, so this is the most orderly quote of the five. Sector read-through is limited — there is no clean peer moving with it today, and the broader EV/battery complex is not a named leader or laggard on the current sector table, so this is close to a single-name drift inside a risk-off tape.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: The raised FY outlook is mildly structural, but a one-cent EPS miss on an unprofitable small cap is not a thesis event in either direction, and the name sits in no favored sector under the current defensive rotation. There is no durable catalyst to hold for, so this is a days-horizon drift, not a swing thesis.
gappers.opportunity_cost: With 0 positions there is nothing to sell, so the real cost is relative: AMPX would consume one of three weekly slots and roughly 20% of equity at the cap, while offering the weakest catalyst on the board — a three-day-stale earnings reaction with a mixed print. Ranked against today's own list it is strictly behind LUNR, which at least has a fresh, idiosyncratic, same-morning catalyst. On R:R, ATR(14) is $0.757, or 8.9% of price, putting the mandated 10% trailing stop at 1.12 ATR — inside the noise band again. A 2:1 target needs +20% to ~$9.61, about 2.1 ATR, which the $23.14 average analyst target makes defensible on a long horizon but which has no near-term catalyst to drive it now that earnings are behind it. Marginal at best and it does not clear 2:1 against a 10% stop.

gappers.catalyst: No issuer-specific negative — an ETH-treasury proxy tracking crypto lower (ETH ~-3.9%, BTC ~-3.6%) at roughly 2x beta, on the same day it disclosed ETH holdings above 6 million tokens.
headlines: Bitmine Immersion Technologies (BMNR) Announces ETH Holdings Reach over 6 Million Tokens with Total Crypto, Cash & Marketable Securities Holdings of $17.2B; ~4.9% of ETH supply (TMX Money, Nov 12)
Bitmine stock rises after ETH holdings exceed $1 billion (Investing.com, earlier)
ETH 2,042.21 -3.85% / BTC-USD 71,293.76 -3.56% on the session (MSN / Benzinga tape)
gappers.catalyst_detail: There is no adverse company announcement. BitMine Immersion disclosed today that its ether holdings passed 6 million tokens, about 4.9% of total ETH supply, with total crypto, cash and marketable securities of $17.2B. The stock is nevertheless down 5.8% because it functions as a levered ETH treasury vehicle and the underlying is falling: ETH is around $2,042, off roughly 3.9% on the session, with BTC near $71,294, off about 3.6%. The 5.8% equity move against a 3.9% move in the asset is close to the ~2x beta the 07:12 ET scan logged for this name earlier today, when it was -5.04% against ETH -2.4%.
gappers.why: Pure NAV mechanics with leverage, not a company event. BMNR's equity is a claim on a crypto balance sheet, so its price is ETH's price geared up by the market's willingness to pay a premium or discount to that NAV. When ETH falls, both legs move against the holder: the asset value drops and the premium compresses as risk appetite fades. The 6M-token disclosure is a position update, not a catalyst — it tells you the size of the exposure, which is precisely why the stock is falling faster than the coin.
gappers.impact: Volume at 5.3M shares is moderate and the quote is tight ($18.08/$18.09), so this is an orderly beta move rather than a dislocation. It is not a headline spike that mean-reverts on its own, because nothing about BMNR is driving it — it will mean-revert if and only if ETH does, which makes any position here a crypto directional bet wearing an equity ticker. The read-through is the broader risk-off tape rather than a sector: BTC -3.6%, GLD -2.62%, VIX 18.33 (+4.8%), SPY -0.21%, with 6 of today's 7 qualifying gappers red. BMNR is also the weakest name on the board on trend, -11.5% over five sessions and -13.6% over twenty, so the beta has been working against it for a month.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: The only driver is ETH's direction, which is not a structural thesis the rulebook can underwrite, and the name is in a confirmed month-long downtrend. There is no M&A, guidance reset, contract or regime change to hold for, so it fails the LONG_TERM test outright.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Nothing to displace, but this is the third time today BMNR has surfaced and been passed over (it ranked #3 on the 07:12 ET scan at -5.04%), and a slot spent here buys crypto beta rather than equity edge — the strategy is a stocks-only momentum book, and sector-momentum rules cannot be applied to a name whose sector is effectively 'ether'. R:R is the least-bad of the five and still fails: ATR(14) is $1.411, or 7.3% of price, the lowest ATR% on the board, which puts the 10% trailing stop at 1.37 ATR — the only one meaningfully outside a one-day range, but still well inside a two-day move for a crypto proxy. A 2:1 target needs +20% to ~$21.74, about 2.6 ATR, against a name that has fallen 13.6% in twenty sessions and whose upside depends entirely on an ETH reversal nobody on this desk is forecasting. Buying a downtrending 2x-beta proxy into a risk-off tape is the opposite of the documented defensive rotation.
